/planning-a-school-trip-to-italy/.heading: Planning a school trip to Italy
/planning-a-school-trip-to-italy/.intro: Start with what your pupils should learn, then build the residential around it. This checklist explains the decisions, responsibilities and information that help EcoWise Italy prepare a useful proposal in Piemonte.
/planning-a-school-trip-to-italy/.imageAlt: Hands-on exploration of a river landscape with EcoWise Italy

sections.heading: 1. Decide what the trip should achieve
paragraphs: A strong residential starts with a learning question rather than a list of attractions. Is the priority field science, ecology, creative expression, teamwork or a balance of these? Share the course or year group and the outcomes you want pupils to take back into school.

EcoWise Italy combines practical investigation and theoretical learning with storytelling, environmental art, nature awareness and group challenges. Teachers can discuss a focused science programme or a broader outdoor-learning journey; not every activity needs to appear in every trip.

sections.heading: 2. Choose a realistic duration
paragraphs: Five days and four nights is the recommended starting point for schools travelling internationally. It gives the group time to settle in, explore, investigate and reflect. Seven-day and multi-week programmes can create a deeper immersion; shorter residentials and day programmes remain possible.

Allow for your actual arrival and departure times. A five-day visit does not automatically mean five full activity days. Agree the working programme with Adam once the travel outline and pupil needs are known.

sections.heading: 3. Bring the group information you already know
paragraphs: A typical class is 20–30 pupils, and programmes can be discussed for approximately 15–80 students. Share approximate ages, numbers and accompanying adults. The usual planning baseline is one accompanying adult per ten pupils, with the final requirement confirmed for the ages, activities and site.

You do not need every answer before enquiring. A school name, contact email and a short description of your aims are enough to begin. Avoid sending pupil names, medical records or other sensitive information in the first enquiry.

sections.heading: 4. Separate programme, accommodation and travel
paragraphs: EcoWise Italy designs and delivers the educational programme, chooses the location, checks availability and books suitable accommodation and food on the school's behalf. That coordination is included in its service, not a separate EcoWise booking fee.

The school normally arranges its main travel. Local transport can sometimes be coordinated by agreement. In the direct model, the school normally pays three separate invoices: EcoWise Italy's programme, accommodation and food, and travel. Do not assume these services form a single protected travel package.

sections.heading: 5. Discuss evidence and responsibilities before approval
paragraphs: Ask for the information your school's approval process requires. EcoWise Italy holds public liability insurance; evidence can be supplied privately to genuine enquiries. Discuss the activities, group needs, supervision responsibilities and programme location before agreeing the visit.

EcoWise Italy does not provide travel insurance. ATOL financial protection, where applicable to a travel booking, is separate from travel insurance. If your school needs one packaged arrangement, an appropriate tour operator can discuss the travel contract and supplier responsibilities with Adam. No package protection should be assumed from this guide.

sections.heading: 6. Treat dates and prices as provisional
paragraphs: Programmes can operate throughout the year, subject to confirming the dates, location and group fit. November–March has historically offered greater flexibility, but that is not a live availability calendar. Spring, summer and autumn programmes can also be discussed.

Prices are bespoke per person and depend on the programme and group. Ask for a written proposal that makes the duration, activities, invoice responsibilities and any exclusions clear. This guide does not quote a fixed price or reserve dates.

sections.heading: 7. Make field science specific to the course
paragraphs: For biology or environmental studies, discuss the course, intended investigations and field methods with Adam. The teacher should confirm the current assessment requirements and how the visit supports pupils' learning. No provider can promise a particular assessment result.

EcoWise Italy's October 2026 public report describes its tenth annual five-day science visit with Beau Soleil College, including terrestrial and aquatic sampling and data collection for DP biology and environmental studies projects. It is a practical example of the programme's use, not an endorsement of every proposed trip.

/school-travel-partners/.heading: A local education partner in Piemonte
/school-travel-partners/.intro: Bring locally delivered field science, outdoor education and imaginative exploration into your school-travel portfolio. EcoWise Italy is interested in conversations with operators whose groups need more than a standard sightseeing itinerary.
/school-travel-partners/.imageAlt: EcoWise Italy outdoor learning in a river landscape

sections.heading: The programme EcoWise Italy can deliver
paragraphs: Adam Rose designs and delivers tailored programmes combining environmental science and ecology with practical investigation, teamwork, storytelling, environmental art and nature awareness. Learning aims and group needs drive the programme, rather than a fixed list of excursions.

A five-day/four-night residential is a useful starting point for an international school group. Shorter visits, seven-day stays and multi-week formats are possible. Programmes can be discussed throughout the year, with dates and local capacity checked individually.

sections.heading: A relevant field-science example
paragraphs: EcoWise Italy's October 2026 public report describes its tenth annual five-day science trip with Beau Soleil College: interdisciplinary science, terrestrial and aquatic sampling, and data collection for DP biology and environmental studies projects.

For a new school, discuss the course, learning objectives and field methods with Adam. Teachers confirm the current assessment requirements so the programme can support their pupils' actual learning priorities.

sections.heading: Local delivery, with responsibilities agreed
paragraphs: EcoWise Italy can design and deliver the educational programme, select appropriate sites and coordinate bookings for accommodation and food. In the direct school model those services are normally invoiced separately from the programme and travel.

An operator relationship needs its own written agreement covering travel contracting, package responsibilities, supplier payments, communications and programme delivery. EcoWise Italy does not hold an ATOL licence or provide travel insurance. Any protection offered through a partner must be described by that partner accurately for the actual arrangement.

sections.heading: What helps establish a useful fit
paragraphs: Please outline your school or group market, typical ages and group sizes, educational focus, trip lengths and the seasons you are considering. A typical EcoWise Italy class is 20–30 pupils, with programme discussions for approximately 15–80 students.

Adam can discuss local delivery, practical planning and a bespoke quote. Insurance evidence is supplied privately to genuine enquiries. Supplier onboarding, safeguarding requirements, cancellation terms and any programme-specific supervision arrangements need to be resolved before a school offer is made.

sections.heading: Explore a working partnership
paragraphs: EcoWise Italy is open to discussing a suitable commercial relationship with a relevant partner. Programme scope, pricing, commercial terms and any allocation are agreed directly with Adam around the groups you serve.

The next step is a short conversation about programme fit and how the working relationship would operate. Adam handles the response directly; an enquiry does not create a booking or supplier contract.
